Arc Barb defaults are length=+1.5pt 2, width'=+0pt 2, and line width=+0pt 1 1. Setup halves arc before evaluating sin/cos, sets tip/visual-back/line/back extents, subtracts half the arrow stroke from length and one arrow stroke from width, then strokes an elliptically scaled arc. Harpoon retains one half and joins it to the shaft; reversed reflects the tip, left/right select the retained side, round changes cap and join, and slant shears the tip. The fixture combines the manual's documented parameter families at 120, 135, and 210 degrees. Parenthesis is exactly Arc Barb[arc=+120,length=+1.725pt +2.3], with round and reversed passed through to that base tip.

Fixed dimensions and dependency factors are resolved against the active path and inner/outer line widths before arrow setup. Start-tip assembly applies endpoint reversal, while explicit reversed exchanges the x extents; harpoon and side selection control y reflection. The resulting line end shortens each straight or curved shaft along its terminal tangent.
Arc paths are approximated by cubic Bezier segments in the local coordinate system. Arc Barb first scales its unit-radius path independently by its adjusted length and half-width.

/usr/local/texlive/2025/texmf-dist/doc/g.findings: The Barbed Arrow Tips examples define the comparison set used by this driver: changed arc, independent length/width/stroke, reversal, round caps, slant, sided harpoons, and color. The manual states that open and fill have no effect and warns that Arc Barb is not correct on double lines; neither unsupported combination is used here. It also describes Parenthesis as a harmonized Arc Barb bow rather than a text glyph.
A to operation installs a curved path from its out and in directions; terminal arrow geometry follows the final tangent, while the intervening node is placed on the completed curve.
